- Middle ring: C (615,652), C (885,652), C (1020,886), C (885,1120), C (615,1120), C (480,886). That is 6 atoms.

The two nitrogens each bond to one of the central carbons (615,652 and 885,652), which are joined to each other. The molecule is symmetric, with the two N atoms on the same side.

c1cnc2c(c1)ccc1cccnc12

- c(c1): the next fusion carbon (480,886), with branch c1 closing the left ring. The left ring is c1, c, n, c2, c(fusion), c1, which is 6 atoms.

text:
I read the structure in three parts and then assigned the stereocentre from the hashed bond.

- **Centre:** a 2,3-dihydro-1H-indene (indane). The oxadiazole sits on the benzene ring, and the five-membered ring carries an NH on its benzylic carbon.

The indane C1 (the NH-bearing carbon) has a hashed bond to N, so N points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.

text:

Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving clockwise, which is (R).

I wrote the SMILES with `[C@@H]` for the order C4, H, NH2, C2 and checked that this gives R.

name: Aldrin
text:
I read the drawing as a chlorinated bis-methano-bridged naphthalene core (the aldrin/isodrin skeleton), and the SMILES below describes it atom for atom.

**Skeleton**
- The left half is a norbornene unit. A C=C (the left vertical bond) sits between two bridgehead carbons that each carry a wedged H. A CH2 bridges those two bridgeheads.
- The two central ring-fusion carbons are joined by a vertical bond, and each carries a hashed H.
- The right half is a second bicyclic unit. Its C=C bears one Cl on each carbon.
- The right bridge carbon carries two Cl.
- The two right bridgeheads each carry a hashed Cl.

**Stereochemistry**
- I assigned `@`/`@@` from the wedge and hash bonds on the six stereocentres: the two H-bearing bridgeheads on the left, the two H-bearing fusion carbons, and the two Cl-bearing bridgeheads on the right.
- Each assignment came from the 2D positions of the neighbours together with whether the H or Cl is drawn toward or away from the viewer.

name: Alphaxalone
text:

name: Alpha-Galactosylceramide
text:

- **Sphingoid base:** the glycosidic oxygen sits on a CH2 (C1). C2 carries the amide nitrogen. C3 and C4 each carry an OH, which gives a phytosphingosine core. From the picture I counted a tail of 14 further CH2/CH3 carbons after C4, which makes the base C18.
- **Acyl group:** the amide carbonyl is followed by a long straight chain. Counting zigzag vertices gave 25 carbons beyond the carbonyl carbon, so the acyl group is C26 (cerotoyl).

name: Alprazolam
text:
This structure matches alprazolam: a triazolobenzodiazepine with a methyl on the triazole, a chlorine on the benzo ring, and a phenyl group on the diazepine ring.

**Triazole ring:** The methyl-bearing carbon (C) is bonded to N (the bridgehead N) and double-bonded to N (the left N). That N connects to the lower N, which is double-bonded to the carbon at the ring fusion. This carbon is also bonded to the bridgehead N. The ring is therefore C(C)=NN=C–N.

**Diazepine ring:** The bridgehead N bonds to an aromatic carbon. The fusion carbon at the ring fusion connects through CH2 to N, which is double-bonded to C(Ph). C(Ph) attaches to the other aromatic fusion carbon.

name: Altiratinib
text:
I read the structure region by region, from left to right.

- **Left end:** a cyclopropyl group attached to a C(=O) that is bonded to NH. This is a cyclopropanecarboxamide.

- **Central benzene:** the pyridine C4 is linked through an ether O to the central benzene. The benzene carries two fluorines and an NH.

- **Right side:** the NH is bonded to C(=O), which is bonded to a cyclopropane quaternary carbon. That carbon also carries a second C(=O)NH-aryl group, where the aryl is 4-fluorophenyl.

Check of the central ring: c2 (O attached), then c (CH), then c(F), then c(N...), then c (CH), then c2F. The ring closure atom bears F and is adjacent to the O-bearing carbon, which matches the drawing.

name: Alverine

name: Alvelestat

name: Alpha-Amanitin
text:
This is my reading of the drawing, written as a SMILES. It is a bicyclic amatoxin-type peptide (it looks like α-amanitin). I traced the ring from the Ile residue around the macrocycle and assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

name: Amdinocillin
text:

name: Alvimopan
text:

name: Aminoglutethimide
text:

name: Amenamevir
text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Oxadiazole ring (left):** The atoms are O, then CH, then N, then C (attached to the phenyl), then N, closing back to O. Going round the ring: O1–C(H)=N–C(Ar)=N–O1. The O is bonded to a CH and to an N, and the N is bonded to the C bearing the aryl group. So the ring is c1ncon1 style, which is a 1,2,4-oxadiazole with the aryl at position 3.

SMILES for the ring and phenyl: c1nc(-c2ccc(...)cc2)no1.

**Para-substituted phenyl:** One end carries the oxadiazole and the other carries NH–C(=O)–CH2–N.

**Central amide nitrogen:** This N carries three groups: the CH2, a 2,6-dimethylphenyl ring, and a C(=O) attached to the thiane ring.

**Thiane ring:** The carbonyl carbon is attached to a ring CH. The ring is CH, CH2, CH2, S(=O)(=O), CH2, CH2, back to CH, so it is a 1,1-dioxothian-4-yl group.

Full SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(cc1)-c1ncon1)CN(c1c(C)cccc1C)C(=O)C1CCS(=O)(=O)CC1

I checked the oxadiazole connectivity. In the drawing, C(H) is bonded to O and double-bonded to N. That N is bonded to C3, which is bonded to the aryl group. C3 is double-bonded to the second N, which is bonded to O. In c1ncon1 notation, c1 (attached to aryl) – n – c – o – n1 would give the aryl carbon between two N atoms. That is the wrong order for this ring. The correct ring is c1(aryl)noc n1: the aryl carbon is bonded to N (which bonds to O) and to the other N (which bonds to CH). Written out: c1(-Ar)noc n1, which is c1(-Ar)nocn1.

Corrected SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(cc1)-c1nocn1)CN(c1c(C)cccc1C)C(=O)C1CCS(=O)(=O)CC1

name: Amiloride
text:
This is amiloride. The drawing shows a pyrazine ring with these substituents:

- C–NH2 (top left of the ring)
- N (top)
- C–NH2 (right)
- C–Cl (bottom right)
- N (bottom)
- C bearing the carbonyl (left)

The carbonyl carbon is C(=O), attached to N=C(N)N, a guanidine group.

I wrote the SMILES by walking around the ring from the carbonyl-bearing carbon: C(=O)(N=C(N)N) is attached to c1, then c(N) (the top-left NH2 carbon), then n, then c(N), then c(Cl), then n closing the ring.

SMILES: NC(N)=NC(=O)c1nc(Cl)c(N)nc1N

Checking the ring order: c1 (bearing C=O), then the top-left carbon with NH2 (c(N)), then N (top), then the right carbon with NH2, then the carbon with Cl, then N (bottom), back to c1. Written this way the ring is c1(C=O) c(N) n c(N) c(Cl) n, which gives c1c(N)nc(N)c(Cl)n1.

Rewriting with that order: NC(N)=NC(=O)c1nc(Cl)c(N)nc1N. The ring runs c1, n, c(Cl), c(N), n, c1(N). That means c1 is bonded to the bottom N, then to C-Cl, then to the right C-NH2, then to the top N, then to the top-left C-NH2, which closes back to c1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(N)=NC(=O)c1nc(Cl)c(N)nc1N

name: Amitraz
text:
This is the amitraz structure: N,N'-bis(2,4-dimethylphenyl)-N-methylformamidine, drawn as a central N-methyl nitrogen flanked by two CH=N–aryl arms.

**Left arm.** The imine N (at 465,650) is bonded to the aromatic carbon at (368,750). That ring carbon is adjacent to a carbon at (230,716) bearing a methyl (the ortho position). The ring continues through (133,818), then (172,954), which carries a methyl (the para position), then (310,987) and (406,885), and back to (368,750). The ring is therefore 2,4-dimethylphenyl.

**Right arm.** The imine N (at 877,748) is bonded to the ring carbon at (1014,781). Its neighbor at (1053,917) bears a methyl (ortho), and the carbon at (1287,849) bears a methyl (para). This is also 2,4-dimethylphenyl.

**Centre.** The central N carries a methyl and is bonded to two carbons, each double-bonded to an imine N (CH=N–aryl).

name: Amosulalol
text:
The drawing is read in three parts.

**Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying a sulfonamide (S(=O)(=O)NH2), a methyl group, and the side chain. Going around the ring, the sulfonamide-bearing carbon at about (317,770) is adjacent to both the methyl-bearing carbon at (300,885) and the carbon at (425,728). The carbon at (425,728) is adjacent to the side-chain-bearing carbon at (514,798). name: Amodiaquine Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing is amodiaquine dihydrochloride dihydrate, so I wrote it as one SMILES with each component separated by dots.

**Main molecule**
- The left part is a diethylaminomethyl group, CH2N(Et)2, attached to a benzene ring.
- On that ring, the CH2 group sits ortho to the OH, and the NH sits para to the OH.
- The NH links to C4 of a 7-chloroquinoline. In the drawing, the ring nitrogen is at the top, the carbon bearing the NH is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon, and Cl is on the benzo ring.

**Quinoline numbering check**
- N1 is the ring nitrogen, C2 and C3 follow, and C4 carries the NH.
- C4a is the fusion carbon next to C4. From C4a the benzo ring runs C5, C6, C7 (bearing Cl), C8, then C8a, which bonds to N1.
- In the drawing, C8a connects to C8 at the upper right, and C8 connects to C7, which carries Cl. This matches 7-chloro.

**SMILES for the amodiaquine core**
CCN(CC)Cc1cc(Nc2ccnc3cc(Cl)ccc23)ccc1O

The quinoline part reads c2ccnc3cc(Cl)ccc23: c2 is C4, then c (C3), c (C2), n (N1), c3 (C8a), c (C8), c(Cl) (C7), c (C6), c (C5), c23 (C4a). This is correct.

**Salt and hydrate components**
The drawing also shows two HCl and two H2O, which I added as separate fragments.

SMILES: CCN(CC)Cc1cc(Nc2ccnc3cc(Cl)ccc23)ccc1O.Cl.Cl.O.O

name: Amorolfine
text:
I read the molecule as amorolfine, which has a cis-2,6-dimethylmorpholine ring.

- **Left end:** a tert-amyl group (CCC(C)(C)–) sits on a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Linker:** from the ring, a CH2 leads to a CH(CH3), then a CH2, then the morpholine nitrogen.
- **Morpholine ring:** N, CH2, C(CH3), O, C(CH3), CH2, closing back to N. Both ring methyls are drawn with hashed bonds, so each carbon bearing a methyl is a stereocentre.
- **Stereo assignment:** I worked out each hashed centre from the 2D coordinates, with the methyl pointing away from the viewer and the hydrogen towards it. Written as N–CH2–C–O–C–CH2, both centres come out as `@`. Both methyls point the same way, so the ring is cis.
- **Unmarked centre:** the CH(CH3) in the linker is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
